quizName:
DMV Practice Test  #6
										  					
  

30 Questions • Passing Score 24

questions.question: Traffic signals sometimes show arrows to control turns from specific lanes. A green arrow:

options.text: Is used only on one-way streets.
Means the same as a circular green light, but you must turn in the direction the arrow points.
Means you may proceed only if the green arrow is with a circular green light.
Points the way to an airport.

questions.correctAnswerText: Means the same as a circular green light, but you must turn in the direction the arrow points.
questions.explanation: A green arrow means the same as a circular green light. However, traffic in that lane must turn in the direction shown by the arrow.

questions.question: You must stop for a school bus:

options.text: That is parked on the road shoulder with no children in it.
When it approaches you, even if its lights are not flashing.
On a two-lane road when its red lights are flashing.
Whenever the driver waves at you.

questions.correctAnswerText: On a two-lane road when its red lights are flashing.
questions.explanation: You must stop when you see a school bus with flashing red lights. On a two-lane road, cars going both directions must stop and stay stopped while the red lights flash or the stop arm is out.

questions.question: You are driving uphill and approaching a heavy truck from behind. You should know that:

options.text: The truck may be traveling slower than the posted speed limit.
You may not be able to safely pass the truck.
You may not be able to legally pass the truck.
All of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: Large trucks often travel slower than the speed limit, especially going uphill. Be careful when approaching from behind. On hills where you cannot see far ahead, it is illegal to pass another vehicle.

questions.question: Lanes of traffic moving in opposite directions are divided by ____ lines.

options.text: White
Red
Black
Yellow

questions.correctAnswerText: Yellow
questions.explanation: Yellow lines divide traffic moving in opposite directions.

questions.question: ____ limit your concentration, perception, judgment, and memory.

options.text: Only alcohol above the legal limit can
Alcohol does not
Even a small amount of alcohol can
Only alcohol above 0.05 percent can

questions.correctAnswerText: Even a small amount of alcohol can
questions.explanation: Even a small amount of alcohol reduces your concentration, perception, judgment, and memory. Your driving skills will suffer. No one can drink and drive safely.

questions.question: This sign means:

options.text: Don't drink if you will drive.
Slippery when wet.
Road curves ahead.
A hill is coming.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slippery when wet.
questions.explanation: This sign warns you that the road becomes slippery when wet.

questions.question: When the driver behind you wants to pass, you should:

options.text: Speed up.
Go the same speed.
Slow down to give the other driver room to pass safely and quickly.
Change lanes.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down to give the other driver room to pass safely and quickly.
questions.explanation: Slow down so the other driver has enough space in front of your vehicle to complete the pass. This allows them to pass more easily and in less time.

questions.question: This sign means:

options.text: Trucks under 18,000 lbs. are allowed.
A steep hill is ahead.
A truck stop is ahead.
No trucks are allowed.

questions.correctAnswerText: A steep hill is ahead.
questions.explanation: This sign warns you that a steep hill is coming.

questions.question: A steady yellow light at an intersection means:

options.text: Go.
Yield to other cars.
Slow down and prepare to stop.
Stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and prepare to stop.
questions.explanation: A steady yellow light means a red light is coming soon. Slow down and get ready to stop. If you are already in the intersection or cannot stop safely, continue through carefully.

questions.question: When a driver is tailgating you:

options.text: Move to the right lane if one is open.
If no right lane is open, slow down gradually when the road ahead is clear. This will encourage the tailgater to pass you.
Never brake suddenly.
All of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: If a driver is tailgating you, move to the right lane if one is available. If not, wait until the road ahead is clear and then slow down gradually. This encourages the tailgater to pass. Never brake suddenly, as this increases the risk of being hit from behind.

questions.question: Two solid white lines across a traffic lane mark a crosswalk. As a driver, you should know:

options.text: Drivers have the right-of-way over pedestrians in crosswalks.
Pedestrians in crosswalks have the right-of-way and should be given it.
No one has the right-of-way in a crosswalk.
Pedestrians must stay out of the way of all traffic.

questions.correctAnswerText: Pedestrians in crosswalks have the right-of-way and should be given it.
questions.explanation: Crosswalk lines show pedestrians where to safely cross. You must always stop for pedestrians in a crosswalk.

questions.question: If a driver is worried, nervous, angry, or crying, the driver should:

options.text: Drive normally. Emotions do not affect driving.
Drive faster because they are more aware.
Calm down and focus before starting to drive.
Call a friend to talk while driving.

questions.correctAnswerText: Calm down and focus before starting to drive.
questions.explanation: Strong emotions can distract you and make it hard to drive well. Calm down and focus on driving before you start the engine.

questions.question: If two drivers reach an empty intersection at the same time:

options.text: The driver on the right has the right-of-way.
The driver on the left has the right-of-way.
One driver can go without stopping.
One driver should honk to give up the right-of-way.

questions.correctAnswerText: The driver on the right has the right-of-way.
questions.explanation: If you reach an empty intersection at the same time as a vehicle on your right, yield to that vehicle. You can go when it is safe.

questions.question: A solid yellow "X" over a traffic lane means:

options.text: You must leave this lane. It will soon have traffic coming the opposite direction.
You can drive in this lane normally.
This lane is for left turns only.
You can use this lane but drive with caution.

questions.correctAnswerText: You must leave this lane. It will soon have traffic coming the opposite direction.
questions.explanation: A solid yellow "X" tells you to get out of that lane right away. The lane direction is about to change.

questions.question: When a traffic light turns green, you should:

options.text: Let pedestrians go first.
Speed up as fast as you can.
Back up slowly.
Wait for another driver to wave you forward.

questions.correctAnswerText: Let pedestrians go first.
questions.explanation: A green light means you can go. But first, check for pedestrians and other traffic still in the intersection and yield to them.

questions.question: What does a single dashed yellow line between lanes mean?

options.text: You can pass if it is safe.
Both lanes go the same direction.
You cannot pass.
You can pass even if it is dangerous.

questions.correctAnswerText: You can pass if it is safe.
questions.explanation: A single dashed yellow line means traffic goes both ways. You can pass if there is no oncoming traffic.

questions.question: Many crashes are caused by:

options.text: Driving too fast for conditions.
Checking mirrors and blind spots often.
Yielding the right-of-way.
Keeping a four-second distance behind other vehicles.

questions.correctAnswerText: Driving too fast for conditions.
questions.explanation: Many crashes happen when drivers go too fast. Always drive at or below the speed limit and slow down when conditions are poor.

questions.question: A green arrow and a red light together mean:

options.text: You can only go straight.
You can only go in the direction of the green arrow.
Wait for a solid green light to go any direction.
All vehicles must stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: You can only go in the direction of the green arrow.
questions.explanation: A green arrow with a red light means only turn or go in the arrow direction if the intersection is clear.

questions.question: When an emergency vehicle with siren and/or lights approaches you, you should:

options.text: Pull right and stop.
Pull right and slow down.
Pull right and turn on your flashers.
Stop and let it pass.

questions.correctAnswerText: Pull right and stop.
questions.explanation: When you see or hear an emergency vehicle, pull to the right side of the road and stop right away.

questions.question: You are in an accident and someone is injured. You should:

options.text: Move the injured person away from the accident right away.
Never move an injured person.
Do not move the injured unless necessary. Keep them warm and give first aid if you can.
Stay away from the injured person.

questions.correctAnswerText: Do not move the injured unless necessary. Keep them warm and give first aid if you can.
questions.explanation: Do not move injured people unless they are in danger. Moving them the wrong way can cause more harm. Keep them warm and apply pressure to stop heavy bleeding.

questions.question: When should you signal before passing another vehicle?

options.text: Just before changing lanes.
At any time.
After changing lanes.
Early enough so other drivers know your plan.

questions.correctAnswerText: Early enough so other drivers know your plan.
questions.explanation: Signal early before passing. This gives other drivers time to know what you plan to do.

questions.question: This road sign means:

options.text: Intersection ahead.
Steep downhill grade ahead.
Winding road.
Merging traffic.

questions.correctAnswerText: Steep downhill grade ahead.
questions.explanation: This sign warns you that a steep downhill grade is coming.

questions.question: How does alcohol affect your driving skills and judgment?

options.text: It helps driving skills but harms judgment.
It harms both driving skills and judgment.
It has no effect on either driving skills or judgment.
It harms driving skills but not judgment.

questions.correctAnswerText: It harms both driving skills and judgment.
questions.explanation: Alcohol harms your reaction time and vision. It also affects your judgment about speed and distance. It makes you more likely to take dangerous chances.

questions.question: You hit a parked car and cannot find the owner. What should you do?

options.text: You have done all you need to do.
Stay until the police arrive.
Leave a written note with your name, address, and what happened.
You can leave.

questions.correctAnswerText: Leave a written note with your name, address, and what happened.
questions.explanation: If you cannot find the owner of a parked car you hit, you must leave a written note. Include your name, address, and a description of the accident.

questions.question: How should small children ride in a vehicle?

options.text: They can be safely held by a strong adult.
They are safe standing on the floor in the back.
They will not be hurt in an accident because they are small.
They must never stand while the vehicle is moving.

questions.correctAnswerText: They must never stand while the vehicle is moving.
questions.explanation: Children must always be properly secured in a car seat or safety belt. No adult can hold a child safely during a crash or sudden stop.

questions.question: When turning onto a street with multiple lanes in your direction, which lane should you turn into?

options.text: The lane closest to your previous lane.
The lane marked with an arrow.
The middle lane.
Any lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: The lane closest to your previous lane.
questions.explanation: Turn into the lane closest to where you came from. Do not change lanes while turning.

questions.question: Turning your head to check your blind spot before changing lanes is:

options.text: A bad driving habit.
A good driving habit.
Unnecessary.
Not necessary if you use the rearview mirror.

questions.correctAnswerText: A good driving habit.
questions.explanation: Always look over your shoulder to check your blind spot before changing lanes. Do not rely only on mirrors.

questions.question: How can you help prevent rear-end collisions?

options.text: Avoid sudden stops.
Check your mirrors and blind spots before stopping.
Release the gas pedal to slow down before applying the brakes.
All of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: To prevent rear-end collisions, avoid sudden stops. Release the gas to slow down, then apply steady brake pressure. Check your mirrors before stopping so following drivers see your brake lights.

questions.question: Two vehicles are side by side ahead of you and you are in a hurry. What should you do?

options.text: Drive close behind the left vehicle and flash your headlights.
Drive close behind the right vehicle.
Keep a two-second distance between you and the vehicle ahead.
Switch between lanes quickly.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep a two-second distance between you and the vehicle ahead.
questions.explanation: Always keep at least two seconds of space between you and the vehicle in front. This gives you room to react. Never tailgate, even if you are in a hurry.

questions.question: A police officer tells you to drive through a red light. What should you do?

options.text: Stop and then proceed.
Wait for the green light.
Follow the officer's directions.
Make a right turn.

questions.correctAnswerText: Follow the officer's directions.
questions.explanation: You must obey all lawful directions from police officers. If an officer directs you to go through a red light, you should do so.
